Read town by town where codes are published; evidence for the ledger's statewide ranges, not a per-tract engine input.

Self-reported by municipalities and updated when they tell DCED; some entries may be out of date. Says whether an ordinance or plan exists, not what it allows or when it was last revised. DCED ids are matched to Census county subdivisions by name; unmatched names are listed in the build notes.

Five municipalities read by hand so far, out of about 2,560; all others are unknown. Posted copies can lag amendments. Commercial code hosts (eCode360, Municode, American Legal) are never read: their terms forbid bulk or automated use.

One ordinance. The web record above is the human-readable page; the text itself was read by script from the city's Legistar web API (https://webapi.legistar.com/v1/pittsburgh/matters/31504/texts/35471, version 7, the pinned one; 31504 is the API's matter id, not the web site's). Struck and inserted words are read from the API's RTF marks. The attachment server (pittsburgh.legistar1.com) disallows robots, so no PDF is read. The full Pittsburgh Code is hosted by a commercial code host and is not read.
City guidance from 2022, not the Zoning Code itself (section 14-604(11) is hosted by a commercial code host and is not read); a 2026 amendment could not be checked, so the row stays draft.
